justification: GATE-1 part 2: the brief hardcoded dev_type='dwelling_house' for the capacity engine, so it never reflected the zone's permitted built form (under-reporting R3/R4, and only conservatively safe on R2). Derive dev_type from the densest PERMITTED residential form in lep_land_use_table (per-zone, per-LGA), fail-safe to dwelling_house, so the engine computes the correct permissible yield without ever assuming a prohibited form.

pre_impl.existing_data: lep_land_use_table is the authoritative LEP Land Use Table: 17,353 rows, 32 zones, 25 LGAs (amalgamated names), columns zone/lga/development_type/permissibility (permitted|prohibited|exempt). Verified: R2 permits dwelling_houses (all LGAs) but NOT residential_flat_buildings; R3 permits multi_dwelling_housing; R4 permits residential_flat_buildings. Per-LGA, so council variation is captured.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The audit recommended DevelopmentPermissionsDB.check_development_feasibility, which reads regulatory_provisions and text-matches provision_type for permitted/prohibited — but that column holds extraction tags (provision_height, formal_development standards) with NO permitted/prohibited categories, so it is unreliable. The real source is lep_land_use_table.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: a pure _densest_permitted_dev_type policy + a thin _fetch_permitted_dev_type DB read; both brief assembly paths replace the hardcoded dev_type with the fetched value. No change to the engine's yield maths (GATE-1 part 1 still gates the count by form).
pre_impl.external_source_error: If the DB query errors, times out (5s), or DATABASE_URL is unset, _fetch_permitted_dev_type catches it and returns dwelling_house — the conservative default — so a DB failure can never raise an impermissible yield, only fall back to the safe form.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A - backend only; the dev_type string flows into the existing ConstraintArithmeticResult.dev_type field (already a str). The capacity card stays unexposed.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If the LGA is outside the 25-LGA table coverage or the zone has no permitted residential form, dev_type falls back to dwelling_house — a conservative under-report (1 dwelling), never an over-report. The visible direction is always safe.

functions.name: _fetch_permitted_dev_type
functions.input: the property zone code and the current LGA name from the brief
functions.output: the engine dev_type for the densest permitted residential form, or dwelling_house when none or on error
functions.if_none: missing zone or LGA, no table coverage, or any DB error returns dwelling_house (conservative fail-safe)

functions.name: _densest_permitted_dev_type
functions.input: the set of permitted development_type strings from the LEP Land Use Table
functions.output: the engine dev_type for the densest permitted form per the fixed density ordering
functions.if_none: an empty set or no recognised residential form returns dwelling_house

values: N/A - no regulatory values hardcoded; the permitted forms come from lep_land_use_table and the density ordering is a fixed form taxonomy, not a numeric planning control.

queries.purpose: Fetch the permitted residential development forms for this zone and LGA from the LEP Land Use Table to pick the densest permitted form
queries.where_clause: zone = %s AND lga ILIKE %s AND permissibility = 'permitted' (parameterised; reads the authoritative LEP land-use table, current LGA scope)

break_it.scenario: An R2 low-density lot that does not permit residential flat buildings is assessed
break_it.what_happens: Hardcoding a denser form would over-report an impermissible apartment yield on R2
break_it.how: only permitted forms are considered; with no RFB/multi/dual permitted it returns dwelling_house; test_densest_permitted_dev_type covers the R2 case

break_it.scenario: An R4 high-density lot that permits residential flat buildings must lift to that form
break_it.what_happens: Keeping dwelling_house would under-report the legitimate high-density yield
break_it.repro: _fetch_permitted_dev_type('R4', 'Inner West') with RFB permitted in the table
break_it.how: the density ordering returns residential_flat_building when permitted; test_fetch_returns_densest_permitted asserts it

break_it.scenario: The database is unreachable or DATABASE_URL is unset during the brief
break_it.what_happens: A raised exception would crash the brief or, worse, leave an inconsistent dev_type
break_it.how: _fetch_permitted_dev_type wraps the query in try/except and returns dwelling_house; test_fetch_db_error_is_failsafe asserts the fallback

break_it.scenario: The property LGA falls outside the 25-LGA table coverage
break_it.what_happens: A missing-coverage lookup could return nothing and be mis-handled as a prohibited form
break_it.repro: _fetch_permitted_dev_type('R4', 'Some Uncovered LGA') returning an empty permitted set
break_it.how: an empty permitted set falls through _densest_permitted_dev_type to dwelling_house; covered by the empty-set test

break_it.scenario: Zone or LGA is missing from the resolved planning controls
break_it.what_happens: A None zone or LGA passed to the query would error or match everything
break_it.how: the function short-circuits to dwelling_house when either input is falsy before touching the DB; test_fetch_missing_inputs_returns_dwelling_house asserts both

post_merge.manual_verify: Re-run an R4 address in a covered LGA and confirm the dev_type lifts to residential_flat_building (denser yield); re-run Haberfield R2 and confirm it stays dwelling_house (1 dwelling). The computation-chain reconciliation and labelling polish remain. Engine stays unexposed (#513 unmerged) until those land.
